subject: pooling results from CFAs using different indicators

messages.author: f4f77115f6648fa1
messages.subject: pooling results from CFAs using different indicators
parts:
I think maybe the title says it all but for context:

I am trying to compare how memory for central details in a story versus peripheral details relate to other variables (e.g., verbal ability, short-term memory). 

An issue I ran into is that memory for central details and peripheral details is so strongly correlated that I run into problems. These variables should be strongly correlated but perhaps not perfectly correlated. 

At least one possible reason these variables are perfectly correlated is because the observed variables defining the latent variables are derived from the same tasks. For example, a person reads Story 1, recall's the story as best as possible, and from that we get a peripheral score and a central score. 

Participants read 9 stories, so I had the idea of reducing the correlation between the two latent variables by using a different subset of 3 indicators for the peripheral and central latent variables. E.g., 

Peri =~ story1_p + story2_p + story3_p
Cent =~ story4_c + story5_c + story6_c

But, a priori, I have no reason to prefer any particular set of variables and, additionally, I may introduce systematic error variance (in the example above, order effects).

So, I thought, why not run every possible CFA using three indicators for each factor and pool the results (because of a constraint I haven't mentioned, it ends up being 216 models). 

But how to proceed...I ran the models and stored the results in a list but I don't know of any function that can extract and pool the results. 

I'm also happy to go a different route if anyone has suggestions. 

-David

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: pooling results from CFAs using different indicators
parts:
So you have measured both _p and _c tasks on all 9 stories? Sounds like an opportunity to specify a MTMM model. That would explicitly model both reasons why a pair of tasks can be correlated: same story (9 orthogonal factors) and task-factors are correlated.
